method: Causal Adaptation Gate Testing is a hierarchical counterfactual testing method in which a controlled input change is assigned to its canonical owner, the earliest layer legally permitted to respond, the latest layer by which a meaningful response is required, and the output dimensions allowed to change. Upstream invariants are protected, expected convergence is distinguished from unresponsiveness, and downstream variation cannot compensate for an earlier causal failure.

Hard validity protects the minimum while target coverage remains later in the lexicographic vector.
The latter returns review state and duplication burden instead of a raw-count reward.
The constrained fixture omits infeasible optional work while preserving required responsibilities.
Public-health participation days do not create every-objective frequency.
Copying the primary Week goal misclassifies explicitly secondary-goal sessions.
A required allocated capacity responsibility can truthfully dominate without a strength main.
Opportunity order cannot establish elapsed recovery time.
Profile defaults stay tentative and yield to confirmed current facts.
Set-dose evidence cannot become allocation-frequency authority.
